Cluster C Personality Disorders

avoidant · dependent · obsessive-compulsive personality disorderWhich fear drives the pattern?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Cluster C (anxious or fearful, a pattern present by early adulthood): avoids people but wants closeness and fears rejection avoidant personality disorder; no wish for closeness is schizoid (cluster A); fear often confined to specific situations is social anxiety disorder (social phobia)
  • Needs others to decide and care for them; submissive, clinging dependent personality disorder; order, perfectionism and control the patient sees as right (ego-syntonic) obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD), not obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), whose obsessions are unwanted
  • Psychotherapy first: CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) may help in avoidant; CBT or psychodynamic psychotherapy for dependent and OCPD; screen for and treat comorbid disorders
What it is

Three lifelong, inflexible personality patterns marked by anxiety or fear: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive

Driver

A fear that shapes behavior: of criticism and rejection (avoidant), of separation and of being unable to care for oneself (dependent), of losing order and control (OCPD)

Triggers

Genetic link to anxiety disorders non-modifiable

Rejection or marginalization in childhood may contribute to avoidant personality disorder

Chain

Fear: of rejection, of being left alone, or of losing control a fixed coping style: avoidance, clinging, or perfectionism

Pattern: present by early adulthood, the same at home and work social and occupational impairment

Course: chronic, though it may improve with treatment; depression and anxiety disorders common alongside comorbidity typically means a poorer outlook

Insights

Avoidant and schizoid patients may both work alone at night; the motive decides: the avoidant patient wants people but fears rejection, the schizoid patient does not want them

OCPD is ego-syntonic: the patient sees the rigid standards as right, so there are no unwanted, intrusive obsessions to neutralize as in OCD

Comorbidity and coursetap to open
ComorbidDepression and anxiety disorders are common with all three: screen for and treat themAvoidant personality disorder and social anxiety disorder often occur together
DependentOften stays in abusive relationships
AvoidantOften avoids treatment

Pause point
Shy night guard avoids people; will not date unless sure of being liked Offered as dependent, obsessive-compulsive, schizotypal or schizoid criteria Confirm with a criterion of the same disorder → Avoids new activities for fear of embarrassment
Student loner with flat affect who wants no close friends Offered as avoidant personality disorder or social anxiety disorder Prefers to be alone; no fear of rejection or embarrassment → Schizoid personality disorder
5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: all three Pattern – pervasive and rigid, stable across settings, with impairment or distress · Onset – by early adulthood; symptoms that began weeks ago after a stressor do not qualify · Test – none; clinical criteria decide
Avoidant personality disorder Core – social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, hypersensitivity to rejection · Features – avoids work roles with contact for fear of criticism; will not get involved unless sure of being liked; avoids new activities that might embarrass Criteria count4 or more of the listed features
Dependent personality disorder Core – an excessive need to be cared for: submissive, clinging, fears separation · Features – needs advice and reassurance for everyday decisions; helpless when alone; rushes into a new caretaking relationship when one ends Criteria count5 or more of the listed features
Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder Core – preoccupation with order, perfectionism and control; ego-syntonic · Features – details, rules and lists; perfectionism that blocks finishing; work before leisure and friends; will not delegate; rigid morals; spends little, saving for disasters Criteria count4 or more of the listed features
7Treatment
1

First lineAny cluster C disorder

Psychotherapy

Avoidant: CBT may help reframe beliefs about self-worth and ease avoidance; social skills work in groups also helps. Dependent and OCPD: CBT or psychodynamic psychotherapy. In dependent personality disorder, avoid fostering dependence on the therapist In practiceIn practice: the Merck Manual also lists anxiolytics or antidepressants for avoidant personality disorder, with no placebo-controlled trials, and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), which limited data suggest may help OCPD; the board answer is psychotherapy

2

AdjunctComorbid depression or anxiety disorder

Screen for and treat the comorbid disorder

Common with all three; in avoidant personality disorder it typically means a poorer outlook

8Follow-up
Follow-up decisions
WhenDo or expect
Avoidant, over yearsSymptoms may ease with age; comorbid depression or social anxiety disorder typically means a poorer outlook
Dependent, over yearsChronic course; may improve with treatment
OCPD, over yearsChronic course; insight and engagement in therapy predict a better one
Practice
  1. 29-year-old man brought by his sister, worried he is lonely has wanted a partner for years but declines every invitation sure coworkers find him dull; turned down a promotion to lead meetings no odd beliefs; affect anxious, not flat → Avoidant personality disorder → wants closeness but avoids people, work roles and new contacts for fear of criticism, as a pervasive pattern: avoidant personality disorder; schizoid patients want no closeness, and social anxiety disorder is often tied to specific situations
  2. 24-year-old man brought by his father, who worries he has no friends spends evenings alone with model trains; never dated, wants no partner shrugs when his manager praises his work normal early development; flat affect; no odd beliefs → Schizoid personality disorder → no wish for closeness, solitary pastimes, flat affect and indifference to praise: schizoid personality disorder; avoidant patients want closeness but fear rejection, and autism needs early childhood social deficits with repetitive behaviors
  3. 34-year-old woman at a routine visit; works alone overnight in a warehouse would like a partner but will not date unless sure she will be liked speaks softly; avoids eye contact no odd beliefs; no psychotic symptoms → Avoids new activities for fear of embarrassment → wants a partner but avoids people for fear of rejection, so avoidant personality disorder is suspected; confirm with a second avoidant criterion, avoiding new activities that may embarrass; the other choices are dependent and schizoid criteria
  4. 38-year-old woman brought by her sister after her husband left within 2 weeks moved in with a new partner who pays her bills has always asked her sister what to wear; hates being alone mood not depressed; no self-harm → Dependent personality disorder → a lifelong need for others to decide and care for her, helplessness alone and a rush into a new caretaking relationship: dependent personality disorder; borderline patients swing between submission and rage, and avoidant patients withdraw until sure of acceptance
  5. 45-year-old engineer referred after missing a third project deadline redoes drawings until every detail is perfect; will not let others help says his standards are simply correct; no intrusive thoughts or rituals works most weekends; few friends → Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder → perfectionism that blocks finishing, refusal to delegate and devotion to work, seen by the patient as right: OCPD; OCD has unwanted obsessions relieved by rituals, and schizoid detachment comes from no wish for closeness, not devotion to work
  6. 27-year-old woman with avoidant personality disorder asks for help wants friends but declines every invitation, sure she will be criticized no self-harm, mood swings or impulsivity no odd beliefs or perceptual disturbances; not depressed → Cognitive behavioral therapy → avoidant personality disorder: psychotherapy, where CBT may help reframe beliefs about self-worth and ease avoidance; dialectical behavior therapy is for borderline personality disorder, and a low-dose antipsychotic may help as an adjunct for severe paranoia in schizotypal personality disorder
Pairs with Cluster B Personality Disorders covers the dramatic, emotional or erratic disorders. Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders covers OCD and its treatment. Panic Disorder and Other Anxiety covers social anxiety disorder. Hears Voices or Holds Odd Beliefs covers schizotypal and paranoid personality disorder. Trauma, Stress and Dissociative Disorders covers adjustment disorder.
Transferable rule

In a lifelong anxious pattern, ask what the patient fears: rejection (avoidant), being left to fend for oneself (dependent), or losing order and control (obsessive-compulsive); a patient who simply wants to be alone is schizoid, cluster A.
